question: Something is torn down and built again with what the user regards as the same identity - the same row, the same document, the same field - and it comes back wearing state from its predecessor: a selection that was cleared, a validation complaint that was resolved, a derived figure computed from data that has since been replaced. In a different library in this folder the same arrangement fails the other way: two things the user considers distinct are handed one shared entry and quietly overwrite each other. The common thread is a store of remembered work kept against a key standing in for an identity, where nothing ties the lifetime of the remembered work to the lifetime of the thing it describes, and where equal keys are assumed to mean the same subject. Which files keep remembered work against such a key, and which own the rule about when that memory must be let go?
anchor: Identity-keyed memory with no lifetime tie. reselect weakMapMemoize keys cached results on argument identity; jotai atomFamily keys atoms on a param with an explicit remove; RTK combineSlices caches injected reducers by key; primitives ordered-dictionary maps keys to collection items; zod registries key metadata off schema identity. Only theme reaching zod.
